la:adj:publicus.html:
pūblĭcus (in inscrr. also POBLICVS and POPLICVS), a, um, adj.
contr. from populicus, from populus
,
of or belonging to the people, State, or community; that is done for the sake or at the expense of the State; public, common.
Lit.: multi suam rem bene gessere et publicam patriā procul, the business of the State, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 295 Vahl.): publica magnificentia (opp. privata luxuria),: sacrificia publica ac privata,: injuriae,done to the State,: litterae testimonium,: memoria publica recensionis tabulis publicis impressa,: pecunia,: publicum funus,at the public expense,: defunctum senatus publico funere honoravit,: causa,an affair of State,; also,a criminal process,: in causis judiciisque publicis,: largitiones,: res publica, the commonwealth, the State; v. publicus ludus, : in publica commoda peccare,: incisa notis marmora publicis,.—
Subst.
pūblĭcūs, i, m.
A public officer, public functionary, magistrate: si quis aut privatus aut publicus, etc.,: metuit publicos,the police, .—
A public slave or servant, an attendant upon a college of augurs, etc., ; ; —
publĭcum, i, n.
Possessions of the State, public territory, communal property: publicum Campanum,.—
The public purse, the public coffers or treasury, public income, revenue, etc.: solitus non modo in publico (in public, openly; v. under II. b.), sed etiam de publico convivari, at public cost, : bona alicujus vendere et in publicum redigere,into the public treasury, for public use,: in publicum emere,; : mille et ducenta talenta praedae in publicum retulit,: publicis male redemptis,: conducere publica,to farm the public revenues,: habere publicum,to be a farmer of the public revenues,: frui publico,; : publicum quadragesimae in Asiā egit,: publicum agitare,: pessimo publico facere,to the injury of the State,.—
Transf.: qui hoc salutationum publicum exercet, who receives pay (like a porter) for admitting to an audience, . —
The archives of the State, public records: ut scriptum in publico in litteris exstat,.—
The commonwealth, State, community, city: consulere in publicum,to deliberate for the public weal,.—
Transf., common, general, public (as adj. rare, and mostly poet.): publica lex hominum,: juvenum Publica cura,: usus,: favor,the favor of all,: lux publica mundi,the sun,: verba,common, usual,; ; ; : moneta,current,.— Hence,
Substt. *
publica, ae, f., a public woman, .—
pu-blicum, i, n., a public place, publicity (freq. and class.): NEVE IN POPLICOD NEVE IN PREIVATOD, S. C. de Bacchan.: IN. POPLICO, Tab. Bantin. lin. 3: in publico esse non audet, includit se domi,: summa in publico copia,: epistulam in publico proponere,publicly,: prodire in publicum,to go out in public,: egredi,: carere publico,not to go out in public, to remain at home,: abstinere publico,; : lectica per publicum vehi,: oratio, quam nuper in publicum dedi,published,.—

On account, at the cost, in behalf, or in charge of the State: haud scio mali quid ortum ex hoc sit publice,: AES. ARGENTVM. AVRVMVE. PVPLICE. Bantin. lin. 9: sunt illustriora, quae publice fiunt,: disciplina puerilis publice exposita,on the part of the State, by the State,: publice interfici,by order of the State,: legationis princeps publice dixit,in the name of the State,: publice maximam putant esse laudem, quam latissime a suis finibus vacare agros,in a national point of view,: frumentum, quod Aedui essent publice polliciti,for the State, in the name of the State,: gratiam atque amicitiam publice privatimque petere,on behalf of the public, and as individuals,fin.; : ea privatim et publice rapere,: potius publice quam privatim amicitiam populi Ron ani colere,; : Minucius eandem publice curationem agens, quam Maelius privatim agendam susceperat,: neque publice neque privatim,: ut filiae ejus publice alerentur,at the public expense,: in urbe, celeberrimo loco elatus publice, id. Before the people, openly, publicly, = palam (only post-class.): publice disserere,: virtutem Claudii publice praedicare,: rumor publice crebuerat,; ; .

senses: to value, esteem, deem, regard, consider
la:verb:puto.html:
pŭto, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
root pu, to cleanse; whence putus, puteus, purus, etc.
,
to clean, cleanse (in the lit. sense very rare; in the trop. very freq.).
Lit.
In gen.: vellus lavare ac putare,: pensa lana putata, Titin. ap. : dolia, dub. (al. picare): aurum quoque putatum dici solet, id est expurgatum, Paul. ex Fest. s. v. putus, p. 216 Müll.—
In partic., to trim, prune, or lop trees or vines: vineas arboresque falce putare,; : vitem,; : parcendum vitibus et ideo anguste putandum,; ; ; cf.: putatae vites et arbores, quod decisis impedimentis remanerent purae, Paul. ex Müll.; so, too, in the foll., the passage from : olivetum,: arborem latius, strictius,: vineam,; .—
Trop., to clear up, set in order; to arrange, settle, adjust.
In gen.: rationem or rationes, to hold a reckoning, reckon together, settle accounts: putare veteres dixerunt vacantia ex quāque re ac non necessaria aut etiam obstantia et aliena auferre et excidere, et, quod esset utile ac sine vitio videretur, relinquere. Sic namque arbores et vites et sic etiam rationes putari dictum,: vilicus rationem cum domino crebro putet,: rationes,: putatur ratio cum argentario,: rationes cum publicanis putare,: ideo ratio putari dicitur in quā summa fit pura,.—
Transf.: quom eam mecum rationem puto,think over, consider,.—
In partic.
To reckon, count, compute a thing: colliciares (tegulae) pro binis putabuntur,will be counted,; cf.: si numerus militum potius quam legionum putatur,.—
Transf.
To believe in, regard: id ipsum est deos non putare, quae ab iis significantur contemnere,.—
To reckon, value, estimate, esteem a thing as any thing (= aestimare): aliquid denariis quadringentis,: magni putare honores,: cum unum te pluris quam omnes illos putem,: parvi,: tantique putat conubia nostra,.—
To reckon, deem, hold, consider, count, esteem, etc.: aliquem nihilo,: aliquid pro certo, Matius et Trebat. ap. , A fin.: pro nihilo,: imperatorem aliquo in numero putare,.—With two acc.: turpem putat lituram,: id nil puto,; ; ; ; ; : hominem prae se neminem,.—
To ponder, consider, reflect upon a thing: dum haec puto,: in quo primum illud debes putare,: multa putans,: cum aliquo argumentis, to consider or investigate maturely, to argue, .—
Transf. (as the result of consideration), to judge, suppose, account, suspect, believe, think, imagine, etc. (cf.: arbitror, opinor, censeo): verbum quoque ipsum puto, quod declarandae sententiae nostrae causā dicimus, non signat profecto aliud, quam id agere nos in re dubiā obscurāque, ut decisis amputatisque falsis opinionibus, quod videatur esse verum et integrum et incorruptum, retineamus,: aliquis forsan me Putet non putare hoc verum,: recte putas,: rem ipsam putasti,you have hit the precise point,: nec committere, ut aliquando dicendum sit, Non putaram,I should not have imagined that,; : Cyprus insula et Cappadociae regnum tecum de me loquentur, puto etiam regem Deiotarum,: noli putare, me maluisse, etc.,; cf. ; ; ; : Numidae remorati dum in elephantis auxilium putant,: stare putes; adeo procedunt tempora tarde,one would suppose,; : acies mea videt aut videre putat,: hanc virtutem vestram ultra periculis obicere nimis grande vitae meae pretium puto,; .—Parenthetically, ; Cael. ap. ; ; ; ; 10, 16, 3: atque intra, puto, septimas Calendas,.—Ironically, : ut puto, deus fio,as I think, in my opinion,; : non, puto, repudiabis, etc.,

I think, I suppose, Vat. ap. . —With gen.: quaecumque sunt in omni mundo, deorum atque hominum putanda sunt,.—Elliptically, ; cf. ; ; ; . —Hence, pŭtă, imper., suppose, for instance, for example, namely (poet. and postAug.): Quinte, puta, aut Publi,: puta, tibi contigisse, ut oculos omnium effugias,: puta te servum esse communem,; ; ; ; : si ille, puta, consul factus fuerit,: hoc, puta, non justum est,; cf. P.: ut puta (sometimes also written as one word, utputa),as for instance, as for example,: ut puta novum crimen,; ; ; .

la:verb:pugno.html:
pugno, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and very rarely
a. [root pug-, to thrust, strike, whence pugil, pungo, etc.], to fight, either singly or in armies, to combat, give battle, engage, contend (very freq. and class.).
Lit.: neque sinistrā impeditā satis commode pugnare poterant,: scutum manu emittere et nudo corpore pugnare,: eminus lapidibus,: cominus in acie,: ex equo,on horseback,: de loco, alt. prol. 33: de ponte,: pro muro toto,: ex iniquiore loco,: pro commodis patriae,—With cum and abl.: elige, cum cive an hoste pugnare malis,: cum hoste in acie,.—With in and acc.: ne quis extra ordinem in hostem pugnaret,: in hostem imparem ex aequo pugnabant,: qui contra imperium in hostem pugnaverant,; .—With adversum and acc.: saepe ante paucis strenuis advorsum multitudinem bene pugnatum,: advorsum Gallos,.—With a homogeneous object: magnam pugnavimu' pugnam, Lucil. ap. Don. ; cf.: haec pugna est pugnata,: pugna summā contentione pugnata,; : inclitam in ponte pugnam ... pugnatam, : proelia,; : bella,; .— Impers. pass.: pugnatur uno tempore omnibus locis,the battle is fought, they fight,: cominus gladiis pugnatum est,: ut in mari quoque pugnetur velut e muris,.—
Transf.
In gen., to contend, conflict, disagree, oppose, contradict; usu. with dat. of person, or with cum: pugnant Stoici cum Peripateticis,. —With acc. and inf.: pugnare non destitit, non esse rerum controversiam, sed nominum,: non magno opere pugnare,to contend not very strongly,: noli pugnare duobus,: ne cupias pugnare puellae, (10), 21; cf.: placitone etiam pugnabis amori?: pressis pugnat habenis,: ne pugnet vulgus habenis,: tam eras excors, ut totā in oratione tuā tecum ipse pugnares,you contradicted yourself,. —Of things: pugnat sententia secum,: pugnavit monitis furor,: pugnatura fretis pila,: frigida pugnabant calidis, umentia siccis, Mollia cum duris, etc., cold bodies contended with hot, moist with dry, etc., : humus, Petr. poët. Sat. 123.—
To struggle, strive, to endeavor, take pains, exert one's self for any thing (rare but class.): illud pugna et enitere, ne, etc.,: id ne impetremus, pugnabis,; cf.: hoc solum hoc tempore pugnatur, ut, etc.,: pugnas, ne reddar, Achille, Ruhnk.: pugnaremque collegae, ut, etc.,.—Poet., with inf.: pugnat molles evincere somnos,; ; : incerto pedum pugnat non stare tumultu,; ; cf., of things,.—P. a. as subst.: pugnan-tĭa, ium, n., contradictions, inconsistencies: pugnantia te loqui non vides?; cf. ; .

pugnus, i, m.
root pug-; v. pugil, pugno

la:adj:putus.html:
pŭtus, a, um, adj.
root pu-, to cleanse; whence also purus, putens, pŭto
,
cleansed, purified, perfectly pure, bright, clear, unmixed; usually joined with purus; purus putus, sometimes purus ac putus: putare valet purum facere. Ideo antiqui purum putum appellarunt, Müll.; cf.: putus antiqui dicebant pro puro, Paul. ex Müll.: in foedere ... scriptum invenitur, ut Carthaginienses populo Romano darent certum pondus argenti puri puti. Quaesitum est, quid esset purum putum. Respondi esse purum putum valde purum ... Argentum putum dictum esse quasi exputatum excoctumque omnique alienā materiā carens,: amicula pura puta, procera, etc., Varr. ap. : hecatombe pura ac puta,pure and clear,: Polumachaeroplagides, Purus putus est ipsus,it's the very man himself,: purus putus hic sycophanta est,a sycophant out and out, a genuine sycophant,.—Without purus: sole exorto puto,.—Sup.: quam bonam meis putissimis orationibus gratiam retulerit,my exceedingly pure, brilliant speeches,.

la:verb:purgo.gloss: to clean, cleanse, clear, purge, purify
senses: to clean, cleanse, clear, purge, purify
to exculpate, justify, vindicate, clear someone's name
la:verb:purgo.html:
purgo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
contr. for purigo, from purum ago
,
to make clean or pure, to clean, cleanse, purify (class.).
Lit.: oleam a foliis et stercore purgato,: cum falcibus purgarunt locum, cleared the place, freed it from bushes, etc., ; : arva longis ligonibus,: domum muribus,: fossas,: proprios leniter ungues cultello,: cana labra, i. e. to clear or free from beard, : pisces,: segetes,.—Absol.: levi sarculo purgare,.—Mid.: purgor in amni,wash,.—
In partic., in medic. lang., to cleanse by stool, vomiting, etc., to purge: quid scammoneae radix ad purgandum possit,; : si is, qui saepe purgatus est, subito habet alvum suppressam,: qui purgor bilem sub verni temporis horam,: se helleboro,: se per inferna aut vomitione,.—
Transf.
To make even by clearing away, to level, ; cf.: purgare viam proprie dicitur ad libramentum proprium redigere, sublato eo quod supra eam esset,.—
To clear away, remove: rudera,: vermes clavo aëneo,: lapides,: sordes,; cf.: scindit se nubes et in aethera purgat apertum,melts away,.—
In partic., in medicine, to remove or expel by purging, rinsing, etc., to heal, cure: purgatum te illius morbi,: pituitas,: fastidium lauri folio,: suppurationes,: tarditatem aurium,: succus purgat cicatrices et nubeculas (oculorum),.—
Trop., to cleanse, purify (syn. lustro).
In gen.: pectora,: urbem,: amplissimos ordines contaminatos veteri neglegentiā purgavit,: rationes,to clear up, settle, pay,.—
To clear away, remove: metum doloris,.—
In partic.
To clear from accusation, to excuse, exculpate, justify (syn. excuso): ut me purgarem tibi,: QVIBVS DE REBVS VOS PVRGAVISTIS ... QVOMQVE DE EIEIS REBVS SENATVEI PVRGATI ESTIS, S. C. de Tiburt. lin. 3 and 12 (ap. Grut. 499, 12): quod te mihi de Sempronio purgas, accipio excusationem,: cui se purgat,: ego me tibi purgo,; so, Caesarem de interitu Marcelli,: si quis tibi se purgare volet, quod, etc.,: si parum vobis essem purgatus,: velle Pompeium se Caesari purgatum, ne, etc.,; cf. : ea pars epistulae tuae, per quam te ac mores tuos mihi purgatos ac probatos esse voluisti,; : accedebant blanditiae virorum factum purgantium cupiditate atque amore,: factum,: facinus,; : crimina,to disprove,; ; cf. probra,: adulescentem crimine civilis belli,to acquit,: innocentiam suam,to vindicate,: suspicionem,to remove,: ea, quae ipsis obicerentur,to refute,: purget miles, quod vicerit hostem,: aliquem alicujus rei,: se adversus alicujus criminationes purgare,: illi lacrimantes nunc purgare se,.—With acc. and inf.: laborare regem, ut purganti se nihil hostile dixisse aut fecisse, fides habeatur,: qui purgarent nec accitos ab eo Bastarnas nec auctore eo quidquam facere,.—
To cleanse or purge from a crime or sin with religious rites, to make expiation or atonement for, to expiate, purify, atone for, lustrate, = expiare, lustrare (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): di patrii, purgamus agros, purgamus agrestes,: populos,: myrtea verbena Romanos Sabinosque,: pontifices purgantes moenia,: domus purgantur lustranturque,. —With the crime or act as an object: nefas, : crimen gladio,; .—Hence, purgā-tus, a, um, P. a.
Cleansed, purified, pure (poet.): auris,: somnia pituitā purgatissima,: purgatioris auri vena, (cf. ).—
Excused, exculpated: ita fiducia quam argumentis purgatiores dimittuntur, ap. , and ap. Don. .—
Pure, freed from sin (eccl. Lat.): vota purgatiora, , 6, 2: purgatissima ecclesia,: pietas,. —Hence, adv.: purgātē, purely: enucleate dicitur purgate, exquisite,.

A stone curb round the mouth of a well: puteal, περιστόμιον φρέατος, Gloss. Philox.: putealia sigillata duo,; .—
Transf., a similar curb placed round any spot. Thus, at Rome, the Puteal, erected in the Comitium, to commemorate the cutting of a whetstone with a razor by the augur Attus Navius, near the Arcus Fabianus. It was subsequently restored by Scribonius Libo, and was called also Puteal Libonis. Money matters were here transacted. According to others, the Puteal of Libo was different from that of Attus Navius: impositum,; ; : Libonis,; ; .
